Verified 8 public pages (/, /preschool, /recreational, /competitive, /cheer, /about, /college-recruits, /camps) all render correctly with no broken images (0 broken out of ~62 total images across pages, 14 lazy on home). action_items: React warning (non-blocking, but noisy in console): 'Invalid DOM property `fetchpriority`. Did you mean `fetchPriority`?' — In JSX, use camelCase `fetchPriority="high"` instead of lowercase `fetchpriority="high"` on tags in PageHero.jsx and Home.jsx hero image. Every page load emits this warning (~8 times per session).
Minor: Repeated 401 errors on resource loads (likely PostHog session recording / analytics endpoints — not app functional). Not caused by this perf change; pre-existing.
critical_code_review_comments: index.html font preload pattern is correct (rel=preload as=style + onload swap + noscript fallback). Anton + Inter both applied successfully.
@import removal from index.css confirmed indirectly (no FOUC/serif fallback observed).
JSX attribute must be camelCase `fetchPriority` (React 16.14+/19) — lowercase produces console warning. This is a small but visible regression from the performance edit.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all pages render, all images load, fonts apply, contact submits, navigation works)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Performance regression check passed. Only cosmetic issue: `fetchpriority` should be `fetchPriority` in JSX to silence a React DOM property warning. Everything else — fonts, hero, images (incl. lazy), navigation, contact form — is functional on the preview URL. Do not test admin analytics per this request.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional regressions found from the perf optimizations. The single console warning traces to JSX attribute casing (React expects `fetchPriority` camelCase); browser DOM still applies the hint but React logs a warning on every render.
